sources.citation: Donald G. Dutton, Arthur P. Aron (1974). Some evidence for heightened sexual attraction under conditions of high anxiety. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1974) in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Shirley A. Feldman-Summers (1974). Blunders and interpersonal attraction under conditions of dependency. Journal of Abnormal Psychology.
sources.notes: Feldman-Summers & Kiesler (1974) JPSP contemporary interpersonal-attraction attribution study in the same 1974 volume.

sources.citation: Craig A. Foster, Betty S. Witcher, W. Keith Campbell, Jeffrey D. Green (1998). Arousal and attraction: Evidence for automatic and controlled processes. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Quantitative meta-analysis across two-factor misattribution-of-arousal experiments confirming heightened romantic attraction under non-romantic physiological arousal.

sources.citation: Cindy M. Meston, Penny F. Frohlich (2003). Love at First Fright: Partner Salience Moderates Roller-Coaster-Induced Excitation Transfer. Archives of Sexual Behavior.
sources.notes: Naturalistic theme-park replication demonstrating elevated attractiveness ratings among unpartnered riders exiting a high-arousal roller coaster.

sources.citation: Gary D. Marshall, Philip G. Zimbardo (1979). Affective consequences of inadequately explained physiological arousal. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Marshall & Zimbardo's critical replication testing affective valence boundaries of unexplained sympathetic arousal.
